# verify2 — independent re-verification of the 7 fix groups

Author: `verifier2` (task t8). Everything below was re-measured **from scratch**.

* **Own data.** Every dataset in this audit is generated by the scripts in this
  directory, except `auto.dta`, which is read straight from
  `D:\Program Files\StataNow19\auto.dta` as a pandas frame. No fixture, no
  registry, no group's `repro_*.py`, no group's `_data.py`.
* **Own Stata bridge.** `mybriage.py` here (≈180 lines) starts the embedded
  StataNow 19.5 (MP) session and reads `e(b)`/`e(V)`/`e()`/`r()`/data. It does
  **not** import `retest/lib/stata_probe.py` and does not import any
  `retest/domains/*/run.py`. Captured live on **2026-10-24**, Stata
  `19.5`.
* **Own alignment.** Coefficient matching is by name with an explicit,
  hand-checked map per comparison; where Stata's names collide (`var` equation
  blocks, `frontier`'s three `_cons`) the alignment is **positional with the
  order printed in the log**, never silent.
* Relative difference = `max(|westata − Stata| / max(|Stata|, 1e-12))`, the
  BRIEF §2.2 definition. Tiers: A ≤1e-9, B ≤1e-6, C ≤1e-3, D ≤1e-2, E above.
  SEs are `sqrt(diag(e(V)))`; where the item is about the matrix, the **full
  matrix** is compared elementwise and labelled as such.

Reproduce (cwd = repo root, each script starts its own Stata session):

```bat
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\a_discrete.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\b_panel.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\c_limited.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\d_systems.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\e_postest_tseries.py m1
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\e_postest_tseries.py m2
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\e_postest_tseries.py ts
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\e2_postest_tests.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\f_linear_iv.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe retest\fix\verify2\g_regressions.py
```

Archived output: `log_discrete.txt`, `log_panel.txt`, `log_limited.txt`,
`log_systems.txt`, `log_tseries.txt`, `log_postest_tests.txt`,
`log_linear_iv.txt`.

## 0. Verdict at a glance

| Group | Items re-measured | A | B/C (as declared) | B/C **not** declared | **False claims** | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| discrete | 13 (1 not verified) | 9 | 3 | 0 | **0** | trustworthy |
| panel | 9 | 7 | 1 | **1 (`e(rank)`)** | **0** — the `e(df_m)` mismatch was declared | trustworthy with caveat |
| limited | 7 | 6 | 1 | 0 | **0** | trustworthy |
| systems | 9 | 5 | 3 | 0 | **1 regression (`nl` rank guard, §4.1)** | mostly trustworthy |
| postest | 15 | 13 | 2 | **1 (poisson AME point estimate)** | **0** | trustworthy |
| tseries | 11 | 10 | 1 | 0 | **0** | trustworthy |
| linear-iv | 6 | 6 | 0 | 0 | **0** | trustworthy |

"False claim" = the group asserted a number or a behaviour that a fresh Stata
session contradicts. Under that strict reading the count is **zero everywhere**:
no group invented a number. What the table separates out is (i) items graded
below A that the summary did not flag, and (ii) one **behaviour** that got worse
(`nl`).

**Nothing in the "test-only" category (b) was found**: every item whose test was
changed also has a changed number, and for each of them I reproduced the new
number from a live Stata session on data I generated myself.

### 0.1 Two things the Lead must not paper over

(the first is a genuine regression; the second is a scalar mismatch, declared
but unresolved)

1. **`nl`'s new rank guard fires on a model Stata estimates fine, and whether it
   fires depends on the units of the regressor** (§4.1). This is a real
   capability regression introduced by S1's repair. It is not a wrong number —
   it refuses — but it refuses `nl` on a perfectly identified quadratic, and
   `auto.dta` clears the guard by only 1.4x.
2. **`panel`'s `e(df_m)` is 2 where Stata reports 1 under a clustered VCE, and
   `e(rank)` is 3 where Stata reports 2** (§4.2). The group declared `df_m` and
   asked for a ruling; `e(rank)` was not declared. Neither number is aligned,
   and both are scalars a user reads. The `F` statistic itself is correct.

Also worth the Lead's attention but not defects: `postest`'s poisson AME point
estimate is 6.6e-9 (B) even though the summary row quotes an A-grade SE (§5.1),
and `oprobit`'s `e(V)` is 1.66e-8 (B) — the B tier is real, the exact digit is
dataset-dependent (§3).

is the strongest evidence that the "Stata stops at `tolerance(.01)`" story is
not an excuse for a wrong fixed point.

## 2. Regression list

The task asked specifically about six "repaired A, broke B" candidates. All six
were re-measured on data I generated; results:

| Candidate | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `xtpcse` **balanced** panel | **not broken** | full `e(V)` 5.59e-15, se 7.56e-16; and the captain's "no `time=`" regression is gone (no-time ≡ with-time to `0.000e+00`) |
| `teffects aipw` **ATE** branch | **not broken** | b 5.04e-15 / se 5.96e-15 |
| `dfuller` **statistic** | **not broken** | printed statistic −0.9142236030432267 vs −0.9142236030432268 (4 cases, all ≤5e-16); only the printed criticals changed, to Stata's table |
| `ologit` **cut-point estimates** | **not broken** | cut coefficients agree to 8.20e-12; only `e(V)`/SEs changed |
| `logit` **base path** | **not broken** | b 2.57e-10, `e(ll)` rel 0.0, `e(N)` equal, `e(V)` 2.57e-10 |
| `poisson` base path | **not broken** | b 5.64e-11, se 9.62e-12 |

Additional regressions I probed on my own initiative (all clear):

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `qreg` **iid** VCE after the robust repair | ≤3.86e-8 in all six τ×hetero cells |
| **`rreg` under both Stata tolerances** | default 1.29e-16, `tolerance(1e-9)` 8.73e-16 — the fix is not tuned to one stopping rule |
| **`var ..., dfk`** after the ML default switch | se 2.03e-16, `e(Sigma)` 2.77e-16; coefficients identical |
| **`2SLS` cluster** after the LIML repair | 4.16e-14 |
| **non-clustered GMM** after the clustered-W repair | b 1.23e-15 |
| **`ologit predict, stdp`** | 1.95e-12; `stdf` still refused (Stata r(198)); `pr` accepted (Stata accepts it too) |
| **`tobit e(df_r)` with `noconstant`** | 299/299 — the `df_m = rank − 1 − hascons` rule generalises |
| **`xtabond e(instruments)`** | 30 on both sides (Stata prints "Number of instruments = 30"), `e(instruments_difference)=29` |
| **`xtpcse` 12×5 with one regressor** | b 9.20e-14, se 0.0 |
| **ordered-model `margins outcome(k)`** | 1-based; all four categories match Stata's `predict(pr outcome(1..4))`: b rel ≤1.2e-7, se rel ≤4.7e-7 (B) |

## 3. Where a declared tier is a little optimistic (not a false claim)

These are all "the group said B and it is B", but the specific digit does not
travel to another dataset. The Lead should quote the tier, not the digit.

| Item | Declared | Mine | Why it moves |
|---|---|---|---|
| `oprobit e(V)` | 1.54e-8 | 1.66e-8 | residual is Stata's stopping point; on my data the b vector agrees to 7.5e-10 and the curvature amplifies it |
| nbreg `vce(robust)` SE | 3.72e-8 | 9.18e-9 | different dispersion; still B |
| tobit `/sigma` `ul` / both-limits | 1.8e-8 / 5.7e-8 | 1.15e-9 / 3.05e-8 | one clearing A, one not; both inside the declared band |
| zip `predict, xb` | declared 1.1e-6 (B) | **6.50e-6 (C)** | it is a pure linear combination; the error is the *coefficient* error (2.4e-7 on x1), amplified where `xb` crosses 0. Same diagnosis the group gave, one tier worse on my data |
| poisson AME (M1d) | se 3.14e-11 | se 3.14e-11 **but b 6.57e-9** | the group only quoted the SE. The point estimate is B. |

## 4. "False repair" findings

### 4.1 `nl`: the new rank guard refuses a model Stata estimates — and the verdict depends on units

**This is the one finding in the audit that I would not let through without a
ruling.**

`retest/fix/systems/FIXES.md` S1 says the rank test is deliberately strict
because the Jacobian is a finite difference, with tolerance
`max(shape)·eps·s_max / h`, `h = _JACOBIAN_STEP = 1e-5` — i.e. a **relative**
cut-off of `200·eps/1e-5 = 4.44e-9`.

On `auto.dta` that cut-off is just wide enough — **by a factor of 1.4**:
`s_min/s_max = 6.250e-9` against a cut-off of `4.441e-9`. On a plain synthetic
quadratic it is not:

```
y = b0 + b1*w + b2*w^2,  w ~ U(2000,5000),  n=200
Stata:  nl (y = {b0} + {b1}*weight + {b2}*weight^2)
        b = [51.5215777, -1.46574591e-02, 1.37389670e-06]
        SE = [2.56725779, 1.50302561e-03, 2.11115573e-07]      ← Stata estimates it
westata: ConsistencyError: "the Jacobian ... has rank 2 but the model has 3
         parameters (b0, b1, b2)"                                ← westata refuses
```

Multiplying the regressor by a constant — which cannot change identifiability —
flips the verdict:

| `weight` × | `cond(J)` | `s_min/s_max` | `cond` after column normalisation | westata |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | 2.72e8 | 3.68e-9 | 84.07 | **REJECTED** |
| 0.1 | 2.72e6 | 3.68e-7 | 84.07 | OK, se rel 1.91e-11 (A) |
| 0.01 | 2.72e4 | 3.67e-5 | 84.07 | OK, se rel 2.57e-11 (A) |
| 0.001 | 3.25e2 | 3.08e-3 | 84.07 | OK, se rel 6.34e-12 (A) |
| 1e-6 | 1.54e6 | 6.50e-7 | 84.07 | OK, se rel 1.05e-11 (A) |

(the `weight × 1e-6` row shows the verdict is not even monotone in `cond(J)`.)

So the guard is **scale-dependent, not rank-dependent**: the correlation
structure of `[1, w, w²]` is the same in every row (`cond` after column
normalisation is `84.07` every time — the matrix is *not* becoming rank
deficient), yet the absolute tolerance `s_max·4.44e-9` grows with `s_max` while
the true near-null direction does not.

Consequences worth stating plainly:

* `nl` on a quadratic in a natural unit (`income` in dollars, `price` in
  dollars) now raises instead of estimating; `auto.dta` itself clears the guard
  by only 1.4x, so this is not a rare corner. A
  user's first reaction to a `ConsistencyError` on `nl ... + {b2}*x^2` would be
  that their model is unidentified; it is not.
* The behaviour is **unit-dependent**, which is the worst kind of
  irreproducibility: the same economics, two datasets, two answers.
* A scale-invariant test — rank of the column-normalised `J` against
  `max(shape)·eps/h` — makes every row agree (`cond` 84.07 in all five, well
  inside any sane cut-off); that is the fix I would recommend.
* I did **not** find a case where the guard lets a genuinely collinear design
  through: `{a}*x + {c}*z` with `z≡x` is caught, and the estimable subset still
  fits. So the guard is not *unsafe*, it is *over-eager*.

Classification: **(c) repaired A but broke B** — S1's SEs are excellent (3.2e-12)
but the same code path now rejects legitimate models.

### 4.2 `panel`: `e(df_m)` and `e(rank)` under a clustered VCE

```
xtreg y x1 x2, fe vce(cluster id)
Stata:     e(df_m) = 1   e(df_b) = 2   e(rank) = 2   F(1,29) printed but computed with df_b
westata:   e(df_m) = 2   e(df_b) = 2   e(rank) = 3
```

With **one** slope Stata reports `e(df_m) = 0`, `e(rank) = 1` — so the rule is
`e(df_m) = (# reported slopes) − 1` and `e(rank) = (# reported slopes)`, both
*excluding* the intercept and the absorbed effects. westata reports the slope
count for `df_m` and "slopes + intercept" for `rank`.

The group declared `df_m` and asked for a ruling, and its reasoning (Stata's own
`e()` is internally inconsistent there: `F` is computed with `df_b`) is honest.
But **`e(rank)` was not declared**, and `e(rank)` is used by `e(p)`/`e(r2)`-style
consumers. I report it as an undisclosed mismatch. The `F` statistic itself is
correct to 6.5e-16, so no *number* is wrong — only two scalars a user can read.

Classification: **(a) with a documented, undisclosed residual** — needs either a
one-line change or an explicit sentence in the README.

## 5. Things the groups reported that I could not confirm as stated

### 5.1 postest M1d — poisson AME reports the SE, hides the point estimate

`FIXES.md` M1d: "poisson AME（新增覆盖）3.68e-03 → **3.14e-11**". Measured:

```
margins, dydx(weight) after poisson rep78 mpg weight
Stata  b = -0.0002983050   se = 0.0004714768
westata b = -0.0002983050  se = 0.0004714768
```

The SE is A (3.14e-11 — the same digits the group quoted, so they measured the
SE). The **point estimate** is 6.57e-9 relative, i.e. **B**. `at(mpg=20)` is the
same pattern (b 6.83e-9, se 3.51e-10). Not wrong, but the summary row implies
both numbers are A. Should read "SE A / b B".

### 5.2 systems T8 — the "A" is about the Hessian, not about the reported SE

Measured on westata's own optimum: b **9.93e-5** and SE **2.51e-5** — both C.
The group's FIXES text says this explicitly ("A (Hessian 已修好；残余 2.5e-5 归因于停机点)"),
and its `diag(H @ V_Stata)` self-consistency argument for n=500 is the kind of
evidence I would want. But if the summary table is copied into the README, "T8 =
A" would be misleading: a user comparing `frontier` SEs gets 2.5e-5.

### 5.3 discrete M3 — `zip predict, xb` is C, not B

Declared 1.1e-6; measured 6.50e-6. Same root cause the group documented (pure
`Xb`, error inherited from the coefficient, amplified where `Xb → 0`). Tier
should read C.

### 5.4 Items I did not independently verify

Stated plainly so the Lead does not treat this document as covering them:

* `zip/zinb e(p)` (discrete P1-19) — I verified the `e(chi2)` that feeds it, not
  the `e(p)` convention itself.
* `qreg`/`rreg` **separate** `e(sum_adev)` check-function semantics.
* `xtabond` Sargan/Hansen/AR(1)/AR(2) — still absent, as the group declared.
* `vecrank` `trend(rconstant)`/`trend(rtrend)` — unimplemented, as declared.
* `pperron`'s `Z(rho)` row of `r(cvalues)` — I only compared the `Z(t)` row.
* `nnmatch` (S4) — the group itself grades it C and says the remaining gap is in
  `σ²_i`; I did not re-derive Abadie-Imbens, so I neither confirm nor refute the
  C grade, I only confirm it is **not** presented as fixed.
* `postest` M2b truncreg `stdf` (B) and M5's negative-LR case — M5 negative LR
  was exercised (non-nested) and matched; truncreg was not re-measured.

## 6. What the Lead can safely say, and what to say carefully

**Say without hedging** (all reproduced independently, A tier, full matrices
where the item is a matrix):

* discrete D1a/D1c/D1d (`ologit` `e(V)` incl. the slope×cut block and `lincom`
  with mixed slope/cut), D2a/D2b/D2d, D3 (`HC1 = N/(N-K)·HC0` exactly), D4
  (LR→Wald with `chi2type`), D5 (`df_m`/`k_aux`/`rank`).
* panel P1/P2 (`vce(robust)` ≡ `vce(cluster)` **bit-identical on both sides**),
  P3a/P3b/P3c/P3d, P4a/P4b/P4c.
* limited T2 (the `df_r` rule, incl. `noconstant`), T5, T6 (`e(rho)` sign),
  T7 (`rreg` under **both** Stata tolerances, identity holds to 0.0).
* systems S1 (SEs), S1b (rank-deficient refusal), S3 **and** S3' (ATET and ATE
  both 1e-15), S5 (both spellings), S6, S7.
* postest M1a/M1b/M1c/M1e/M1f/M1g (default / `at()` / `over()`), M2a, M4 (all
  four), M5 (5/5), M6, M7 — but quote M1g's explicit `outcome(k)` as B.
* tseries V1a/b/c, V2, V3 (and the statistic is untouched), V3b, V4, V5, and the
  `dfk` switch.
* linear-iv L1, L2, **L3** (GMM cluster: point estimate 1.1e-15 — the single
  biggest functional gain in the round), L4 (all eight VCE/weight cases), L5,
  L6.

**Say with the stated caveat:**

* discrete D1b `oprobit e(V)` — B (1.7e-8); quote "B, Stata's stopping point",
  not the digit.
* discrete D2c nbreg robust — B on SE.
* discrete M3 `zip predict, n/pr/stdp` — B; **`xb` is C**.
* panel P5 `xtnbreg, fe` — B (se 5.2e-8, b 2.7e-9). On my data Stata's default
  and `ltolerance(1e-8)` answers are identical, so the group's "compare against
  `ltolerance(1e-8)`" caveat did not even trigger here; the residual is simply
  the optimiser's last digits.
* limited T1 `ul`/both-limits and T3/T4 — B.
* systems S2 (`nl` starts) — B (9.3e-8).
* systems T8 — **C** at the reported estimates; only the Hessian is A.
* postest M1d poisson AME — **se A, b B**.
* tseries V6 arch — B (~4e-5 on my DGP).

**Say only after a decision:**

* **`nl`'s rank guard (§4.1).** Either scale-invariant rank detection (test on
  column-normalised `J`, or compare against `eps·‖J‖` after scaling) or a much
  smaller safety factor. Until then `nl` refuses identified quadratics in
  natural units. I would not ship "S1 fixed" without this.
* **`panel e(df_m)` / `e(rank)` (§4.2).** `e(rank)` is off by one under a
  clustered VCE with `k` slopes and was not in the group's "needs ruling" list.
* `linear-iv` aweight `e(ll)`/`e(ll_0)`: absolute offset 4.55 on my data, `(ll −
  ll_0)` exact. Pre-existing, not introduced this round — but if the README
  claims `e(ll)` coverage, it needs this sentence.

## 7. Test-suite state (my own run, not the groups')

```
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests -q -p no:randomly --ignore=tests/conformance
   -> 1176 passed
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/conformance -q -p no:randomly
   -> 200 passed
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests -q -p no:randomly            (everything)
   -> 1376 passed
```

(The two "all green" runs above were taken at different moments during my work;
the last line is the final state of the tree and it is fully green.)

Diff discipline, checked mechanically over `git diff tests/`:

* 419 assertion lines added, 22 removed; **zero** added `xfail`/`skip` except one
  `pytest.skip("auto.dta not downloaded")` guard.
* Every removed assertion I inspected is replaced by a *tighter or re-based*
  assertion with a captured Stata constant, not a looser one. The removed
  tolerances (`abs=1e-3`, `rtol=1e-12` on a wrong target, `atol=1e-10`) belong
  to assertions that encoded the *old bug* — e.g.
  `test_robust_standard_errors_match_stata_hc1` asserted HC1 for `xtreg, fe`
  and `test_auto_df_off_reproduces_stata_clustered_standard_errors` asserted
  `auto_df=False`; both are contradicted by the live Stata numbers I measured
  independently in §1.2.
* No test was weakened to make a fix pass: every group's rewritten assertion is
  backed by a number I re-derived from a fresh Stata session.

---

## 8. Bottom line

* **7 of 7 groups' numbers are real** — no group invented a figure, and none
  "fixed" a defect by editing an assertion. Six groups can be quoted as
  reported once the tier caveats in §3 and §5 are attached: linear-iv 6/6 A;
  discrete 9 A + 3 B (declared); limited 6 A + 1 B; tseries 10 A + 1 declared
  B; postest 13 A + 2 B (one of them an undeclared point estimate); panel 7 A
  + 1 declared `e(df_m)` mismatch **+ 1 undeclared `e(rank)` mismatch**.
* **1 item must not be called fixed**: `nl`'s covariance repair is numerically
  excellent but its new guard rejects identified models depending on units
  (§4.1). This is the only place in the round where a *capability* got worse.
* **No case of "test changed, number unchanged"** was found anywhere.
* The three most valuable genuinely-new capabilities, verified end-to-end:
  `ivregress gmm, vce(cluster)` (point estimate now 1.1e-15 instead of 3.6e-2),
  `xtreg, fe vce(robust)` now literally `vce(cluster)` on both sides, and
  `xtpcse, pairwise` which previously did not exist.
